note: Corporate legal work, by who covers it and how. 'Model' matters more than category here: a law firm can give advice and take on liability, software cannot, and the hybrids sit in between. Y = covers it as a core offering, part = partial or adjacent, blank = not covered.

models.hybrid: Hybrid — software plus its own lawyers

providers.name: Pierson Ferdinand
providers.pricing: Partner-rate hourly; partners keep most of billings
providers.note: Partner-only, no associates, 90+ practice areas, ~300 partners. AI (Harvey) explicitly in place of the junior layer.

providers.name: FisherBroyles
providers.note: The pre-AI precedent for partner-only economics — running since 2002.

providers.name: Carta Law (fka Avantia)
providers.note: Fund legal and compliance inside an ERP. A SaaS company that bought a law firm.

providers.name: General Legal
providers.pricing: Flat fee — NDAs $250, contract review from $250–500, negotiation ~$1,000
providers.note: Hires only experienced lawyers — 5th–8th year Big Law or 10–15+ years in-house, no entry level. Expanding from commercial contracts into corporate.

providers.name: Arcline
providers.note: AI first draft, lawyer final revision; ~80% of lawyer work removed, often same-day.

providers.name: AgileCounsel
providers.note: Built cross-border from the start rather than US-first.

providers.name: Moritz
providers.pricing: Flat upfront; AI does ~80%, client pays for the last 20%
providers.note: Same-day turnaround; $2B+ aggregate contract value since early 2026.

providers.name: Crosby
providers.note: Narrow by design: NDAs and MSAs, median 58 minutes to attorney sign-off.

providers.name: Soxton
providers.note: The most legible unbundled pricing in the category.

providers.name: Vector
providers.note: Lawyers and paralegals averaging 10+ years of Big Law experience plus custom AI.

providers.name: Eudia
providers.note: AI plus its own legal professionals, sold to enterprise departments.

providers.name: Ontra
providers.note: Does the negotiating, not just the tooling — AI plus a global lawyer network. Not a law firm.

providers.name: Axiom
providers.note: Senior talent without the pyramid, sold this way for 25 years. AI layer is recent.

providers.name: Manifest OS
providers.note: Infrastructure for firms rather than a firm: first incubated practice is immigration, not corporate.

providers.name: Klea
providers.note: Closest existing product to automated corp sec at global scale — and it is software, not a firm.

providers.name: Athennian
providers.note: Minute books, registers, filings, org charts. The modern default for the corp sec workstream.

providers.name: Diligent Entities
providers.note: Enterprise governance and the corporate record as single source of truth.

providers.name: CSC
providers.note: Registered agent and filings footprint at enterprise scale. Competing on corp sec means competing with this, not just with software.

providers.name: Vistra
providers.note: Has done end-to-end corporate secretarial work across jurisdictions at fixed prices for decades — without AI and without being a law firm.

providers.name: Clerky
providers.note: Has automated startup corporate paperwork from formation onward for over a decade — as document automation, not advice.

providers.name: Carta
providers.note: Holds the corporate record, then bought the legal layer. The convergence pattern.

providers.name: Pulley
providers.note: Cap table; integrates with Clerky so formation flows into equity.

providers.name: Firstbase
providers.scope: Global — US entities for non-US founders
providers.note: Formation plus the operational wrap: address, mailroom, bookkeeping, tax, compliance.

providers.name: Ironclad
providers.note: CLM — workflow and repository for the contract layer, no advice.

providers.name: Spellbook
providers.note: Drafting and review inside Word, aimed at small firms and lean in-house teams.
